market.headline: Stocks point higher for a short post-Thanksgiving session, but the backdrop is still hostile: QQQ is 16.9% off its high and VIX is 26.36. Today's main story is Nvidia pausing server shipments to Southeast Asia while Beijing pumps up Chinese chip stocks.
watch: QQQ 633.93 (Wednesday's close) and 606.23 (20-day low) in a thin early-close session
SPY 730.77 (200-day average): the gap above it would turn the trend back up
Next week: JOLTS Dec 1 at 10:00, payrolls Dec 4 at 08:30
market.if_then: If QQQ slips back below 633.93 in the first hour, then stop buying for the day and stay in cash.

stocks.headline: Nvidia told partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia under tighter US export rules. Last trade 151.22 after hours.
stocks.why: Washington is closing the routes that let AI chips reach China through Southeast Asia. A new rule also makes buyers rule out Chinese renters. That cuts sales Nvidia was counting on, just as the Jensen Huang scandal raises open questions about governance. The business itself is still very strong: sales are up 106%, the operating margin is 65%, and the stock trades at 9× next year's forecast. The shipment pause also hits TSM, SMCI and MU, which sell into the same server chain. Beijing's support rally for Chinese chips does not help Nvidia.

long_term.reason: Earnings power and a 9× forward price argue for owning it. But export curbs and the governance scandal are new risks, so this is not the moment to add.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A short, clearly defined pause plus a management fix would make it Add on dips. A longer ban or forced leadership changes would make it Trim.
stocks.action: Don't buy the open. Stay out unless it gets back above 149.3 and holds it through the first hour.

levels.means: above = the news is absorbed; below = sellers are in control today
above = Wednesday's low holds; below = a retest of the lows is under way
above = the 52-week low still stands; below = the long-term case is broken for now

stocks.if_then: If it trades back above 151.22 and holds for an hour, then drop the bet against it and do nothing.

stocks.headline: Oracle fell 5.1% to 103.88 on Wednesday, a new 52-week low, then traded at 105.84 after hours.
stocks.why: The AI sell-off has hit the most leveraged data-center names hardest, and Oracle is down 58.2% from its high. The business does not match the price. Sales are up 30% and speeding up, the contracted backlog is $664.0B, and the stock trades at 9× next year's forecast. Analysts expect EPS on Dec 14 to be lower than a year ago, and the stock usually moves about 11% on results. Spending on capacity is what investors are punishing, so watch for any capex or funding news before then.

long_term.reason: Agrees with the house view: a record backlog and accelerating sales at its lowest valuation in 5 years. The risk is heavy spending ahead of revenue, not demand.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A break below 99.34, or a December report that raises spending without matching revenue, would make it Wait.
stocks.action: Buy a first half-position if it trades at or above 105.84. Add the rest only after the Dec 14 report.

levels.means: above = buyers are back and the entry is valid; below = no entry today
above = the 52-week low holds; below = sell the starter position
above = the 20-day trend has turned up; below = the rebound is still unproven

stocks.if_then: If it buys in and then loses 103.88, then sell the position before the close.
